name: Manage warehouses and spare parts
summary: The warehouses hold the spare parts and consumables that maintenance needs, including expensive critical spares for the generating units. Storekeepers pick and issue parts against work order reservations, deliver kits to plants and remote sites, receive and inspect supplier deliveries, post receipts so invoices can be paid, and put stock away. The work is slowed and made error-prone by stock records that do not match the bins, which turn picks into searches and stock-outs into emergency purchases, by deliveries that are short or damaged, and by long drives to hydro and wind sites.

baseline.org_archetype: An Alberta generator's central supply chain group running warehouses at the Wabamun-area plants and the mine, with satellite stores for hydro and wind, on an ERP inventory module with paper pick tickets.
baseline.notes: Highvale mine stores carried a large share of issues until mining ended at the end of 2021; volumes after that are lower.

trigger: A work order reservation is released for issue, or a supplier delivery arrives at the warehouse.
end_state: Parts are issued and posted to the work order, or received, posted and put away or staged, or returned to the supplier, or a stock-out is passed to purchasing.

volume.seasonality: Higher before and during spring and fall outages, and in summer for hydro and wind work; mine issues ended in 2022.

surge.cause: spring and fall planned outage seasons

evidence.note: Outage kitting and receipts before and during outage seasons; the multiplier is an estimate below the organisation file's because hydro, wind and mine issues do not surge with thermal outages.

Kept at the organisation file's estimate; roughly consistent with about 1,400 thermal work orders a month, half needing parts, plus hydro, wind and mine issues and 750 purchase orders received. Mine closure at the end of 2021 (aif2021) lowers volume in 2022.
Org file lists 24 storekeepers; the rest of their time goes to cycle counts, preservation of critical spares, returns and outage kitting. Estimate.
Adjustment approvals and replenishment review share of 4 supervisors; estimate.
Supplier discrepancies only; estimate.
Critical spare inspection share; estimate.

systems.name: ERP (finance, purchasing and plant maintenance modules)
Document management and engineering drawings repository

steps.name: Route stock transaction
steps.description: The case is either a reservation released from a work order, which needs parts issued, or a supplier delivery arriving at the warehouse dock, which needs receiving. This step only routes the case.

evidence.note: Issue and receipt shares estimated from the usual ratio of issue lines to PO receipts in MRO stores.

steps.name: Print pick ticket from reservation
steps.description: Released reservations for the next day's scheduled work print as pick tickets in the warehouse overnight; break-in requests are printed when the craftsperson arrives at the counter.

evidence.note: Standard ERP output; wait is an estimate.

steps.name: Pick parts from bins
steps.description: The storekeeper walks the pick ticket through the warehouse, takes each item from its bin location, checks the part number and quantity against the ticket, and notes any bin that is empty or short.

next.condition: bin empty or short against the record

evidence.note: Reliabilityweb reports fill rates under 80 percent in typical storerooms; a generator with critical spares is assumed to find 90 percent of picks (author's estimate).

steps.name: Search for missing stock
steps.description: The storekeeper checks alternate bin locations, open receipts not yet put away, the quarantine area and recent issue history in the ERP to find the missing item or explain the difference.

evidence.note: Inaccurate records are common; practitioners target 95 to 98 percent record accuracy.

steps.name: Recount bin and propose adjustment
steps.description: The storekeeper counts the bin and any alternate locations, compares the count with the ERP quantity, and enters a count document with the proposed adjustment and a reason.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Approve inventory adjustment
steps.description: The warehouse supervisor reviews the count document and the reason, approves adjustments within limits or escalates large write-offs to finance, and decides whether the part was found or is out of stock.

control.basis: Internal control over financial reporting: independent approval of inventory adjustments

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Raise emergency requisition and tell planner
steps.description: The storekeeper creates a purchase requisition for the stock-out marked urgent and emails or phones the planner so the work order can be rescheduled or a substitute found.

evidence.note: Stock-outs drive reactive emergency purchases.

steps.name: Stage kit for the work order
steps.description: The storekeeper bags and tags the parts with the work order number and places them in the staging area for the crew, or in the delivery cage for remote sites.

error.defect_description: Kit staged under the wrong work order.

next.condition: delivered to a plant or remote site

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Deliver parts by truck
steps.description: On the daily run the storekeeper drives a service truck from the central warehouse to plants, hydro stations, wind sites or the mine, drops kits at the site laydown or stores cage and collects returns.

evidence.note: Daily delivery run; share and minutes are estimates.

steps.name: Hand over parts and post goods issue
steps.description: The storekeeper gets the receiver's signature or name, posts the goods issue against the work order in the ERP, and files the signed pick ticket.

error.defect_description: Issue posted to the wrong work order or not posted, so the stock record drifts.

evidence.note: Unposted and misposted transactions are a main cause of record inaccuracy.

steps.name: Check reorder point overnight
steps.description: The nightly materials planning run compares stock on hand plus open orders with each item's reorder point and creates replenishment requisitions for items that fall below it.

evidence.note: Standard ERP reorder-point planning; share is an estimate.

steps.name: Review and release replenishment requisitions
steps.description: The warehouse supervisor reviews the requisitions the run created, checks unusual quantities and items with no recent use, adjusts or deletes them, and releases the rest to purchasing.

evidence.note: A 2025 vendor survey cited there found 22 percent of MRO inventory unused for over five years, which this review is meant to prevent.

steps.name: Unload delivery and check packing slip
steps.description: The storekeeper signs the carrier's bill of lading, unloads with a forklift, and matches the packing slip to the open purchase order in the ERP by PO number, item and quantity.

error.defect_description: Delivery matched to the wrong PO line.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Inspect goods
steps.description: The storekeeper opens the packaging, checks part numbers, quantity and visible damage, and flags items marked as critical spares or pressure parts that need technical inspection or material certificates.

next.condition: critical spare or pressure part needs technical inspection

evidence.note: Shares are estimates.

steps.name: Inspect critical spare and certificates
steps.description: A plant engineer checks the critical spare against the drawing or specification and reviews material test reports and certificates for pressure-retaining parts before the item can be accepted into stock.

control.basis: Company quality procedure for critical spares and pressure-retaining parts

evidence.note: Estimate; ABSA rules for pressure equipment were not opened, so the control is recorded as company policy.

steps.name: Record discrepancy and quarantine
steps.description: The storekeeper photographs the problem, moves the goods to the quarantine area, notes the discrepancy on the PO and emails the buyer with the details.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Agree return or acceptance with supplier
steps.description: The buyer contacts the supplier and agrees either a return for replacement or credit, or acceptance of a partial or slightly different item with a price adjustment, and tells stores what to do.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Post goods receipt
steps.description: The storekeeper posts the goods receipt against the PO in the ERP for the accepted quantity, which updates stock or the work order and lets accounts payable match the invoice.

error.defect_description: Wrong quantity received, causing an invoice block.

control.basis: Receiving recorded by stores, independent of the buyer who placed the order

next.condition: non-stock item for a work order

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Put away to bin
steps.description: The storekeeper labels the item, puts it in its bin location, and updates the bin if it is a new item. Bulky or preserved spares, such as motors and shafts, go to the yard or a heated building.

error.defect_description: Item put in the wrong bin.

evidence.note: Estimate; receipts often sit in the receiving area for a day.

steps.name: Stage non-stock item and notify requester
steps.description: The storekeeper tags the direct-charge item with the work order number, places it in the staging area and emails the planner or requester that it has arrived.

evidence.note: Estimate.

exceptions.name: Short pick
exceptions.description: The bin does not hold what the record says; the storekeeper searches, recounts and gets the adjustment approved.

exceptions.name: Stock-out
exceptions.description: The part is not in stock and an urgent requisition goes to purchasing.

exceptions.name: Delivery to a remote site
exceptions.description: Kits are driven to plants, hydro stations, wind sites or the mine on the daily run.

exceptions.name: Receiving discrepancy
exceptions.description: Short, damaged or wrong goods are quarantined and the buyer agrees a return or credit.

exceptions.name: Critical spare inspection
exceptions.description: A plant engineer checks the item and certificates before acceptance.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from reservation release or delivery arrival to issue posted or stock put away

evidence.note: Author's estimate: next-day picks for scheduled work and same- or next-day receiving, with approvals, remote deliveries and inspections in the tail. No published figure found.

benchmarks.unit: share of stock records matching the bin count

evidence.note: A management target, not a measured average.

pain_points.description: Stock records drift from the bins because issues are not posted, are posted to the wrong work order or parts are put in the wrong bin, so picks turn into searches.
A stock-out found at the pick stops the work order and becomes an emergency purchase.
Remote hydro and wind sites depend on a daily truck run, so a missed kit costs a day.

evidence.note: Estimate.

pain_points.description: Critical spares wait days for an engineer's inspection before they can be accepted.

evidence.note: Estimate.

sources.title: Reliability vs the capricious MRO storeroom
sources.supports: Undated practitioner article on typical MRO storerooms: fill rates of stocked SKUs under 80 percent (out of stock 20 percent of the time); only 50 to 70 percent of planned work orders are filled from stores and 30 to 50 percent cause reactive, emergency purchases; inaccurate inventory quantities disrupt reservations; planners, purchasing and engineers stop their work to chase parts.

sources.title: MRO and spare parts inventory statistics: stockouts, accuracy, costs
sources.supports: Undated review. Practitioners commonly target 95 to 98 percent inventory record accuracy (a management target, not a measured average); no large-scale audit of MRO storeroom record accuracy was found; vendor research puts duplicate purchases at 5 to 7 percent of spend; a 2025 vendor survey found 22 percent of MRO inventory unused for more than five years and about 66 percent of manufacturers managing MRO in the ERP alone.

sources.title: TransAlta Corporation Annual Information Form for the year ended December 31, 2021 (Exhibit 13.1 to Form 40-F)
sources.publisher: TransAlta Corporation via U.S. SEC EDGAR
sources.supports: Forward-looking risk list names disruptions to supply chains, including the ability to secure necessary equipment, and equipment failure and the ability to complete repairs cost-effectively; the partner (Heartland) operates and maintains the Sheerness units; Sundance 4 stopped firing coal from January 1, 2022; Highvale mining ended at the end of 2021; many employees have more than 20 years of service.

assumptions: One case is one pick ticket or one delivery, not one line; a ticket averages several lines.

Cycle counting, preservation of stored critical spares (shaft rotation, desiccant changes), returns and obsolete stock disposal are routine work outside the case flow; they are part of the storekeepers' time not assigned to this process.
The plant engineer and buyer take part in this process although the organisation file lists only storekeepers and the warehouse supervisor.
Service trucks are the organisation file's shared fleet; the stores share is the daily delivery run.
Issue shares by source assume mine stores were still active, as they were for most of the reference period.
